question: Thinking of leaving on day 70 of a 100-day term. Will any of my federal aid be considered unearned?
reference_answer: No. Day 70 of a 100-day term is past the 60% point, and once you've completed more than 60% of the payment period you've earned 100% of the federal aid you received and were scheduled to receive. Your school's own refund policy can still affect what you owe.

question: Bursar told me excess aid gets released 'whenever processing finishes'. Is there any federal time limit on paying me my credit balance?
reference_answer: Yes. Unless you've authorized the school to hold it, a federal aid credit balance must be paid as soon as possible and no later than 14 days after the first day of classes, or 14 days after the balance occurs if that's later.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 4, Ch. 2: Disbursing Title IV Funds

question: For a 60-credit associate degree, how many attempted credits can I have before I hit the federal aid time limit?
reference_answer: The maximum timeframe for undergraduate credit-hour programs can be no longer than 150% of the program's published length, so for a 60-credit program that's up to 90 attempted credits. You fail the standard once it's impossible to finish within that limit.

question: Lost aid for SAP. If I sit out a semester, is my eligibility restored when I come back?
reference_answer: No. Sitting out a term or paying on your own doesn't change your SAP status. You regain eligibility by meeting your school's SAP standards again, or by a successful appeal if your school allows one.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 1, Ch. 1: School-Determined Requirements

question: Will my $3,000 work-study award be credited to my tuition bill in August?
must_include: paid at least once a month
reference_answer: No. Federal Work-Study is paid as wages for hours you actually work, at least once a month, and the award is the most you can earn. It goes on your school account only if you give written authorization, and then only as you earn it.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 6, Ch. 2: The Federal Work-Study Program

question: A foundation just gave me a scholarship after I accepted my package. What part of my aid is most likely to be cut?
reference_answer: Report the scholarship to your financial aid office. If it puts your aid over your need, the school adjusts your package, and federal guidance tells schools to reduce borrowing first, starting with unsubsidized loans. A correctly calculated Pell Grant normally isn't reduced for other aid.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 4, Ch. 3: Overawards and Overpayments

question: Our college refused to adjust my aid for my dad's huge medical bills. Who can I take this to above them?
must_not_include: file an appeal with the Department
reference_answer: There isn't a higher federal appeal: the aid administrator's professional judgment decision is final and cannot be appealed to the Department of Education. You can ask the school why it was denied and whether more documentation would help.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 5: Special Cases

question: I signed something in orientation letting the school keep my leftover aid. Am I stuck with that for the whole year?
reference_answer: No. You can cancel or modify a credit balance authorization at any time, and the school must then pay you the held funds within 14 days. A school also can't require you to sign one.

sources.title: 34 CFR 668.165: Notices and authorizations
2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 4, Ch. 2: Disbursing Title IV Funds

question: My R2T4 letter says I'd owe $40 back on my FSEOG. Do I actually have to pay that?
reference_answer: No. A student doesn't have to repay a grant overpayment of $50 or less per grant program after a withdrawal, as long as it isn't a remaining balance. Confirm the amount with your financial aid office.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 5, Ch. 2: The Steps in the Return of Title IV Aid Calculation, Part 2

question: Taking 9 credits this fall at a semester school where full-time is 12. Can I still borrow the full annual unsubsidized amount?
must_not_include: you can borrow the full annual limit
reference_answer: Probably not. For periods of enrollment beginning on or after July 1, 2026, schools must reduce the annual Direct Loan limit in direct proportion to how far below full-time you are. At 9 of 12 credits that's roughly a 25% reduction, so about 75% of the limit. Your aid office makes the actual calculation.

question: The net price calculator on a college site says I'd pay about half. Is the school held to that number?
reference_answer: No. A net price calculator gives only an estimate, and it must say the result isn't binding and isn't a final award. You have to complete the FAFSA to get an actual federal aid award, and the school's aid offer is what counts.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 2, Ch. 6: Consumer Information and School Reporting

question: I just stopped showing up to classes around October and never filled out any withdrawal form. What withdrawal date will the school use for my aid?
reference_answer: Stopping attendance without notifying the school is an unofficial withdrawal. The school can use the midpoint of the payment period as your withdrawal date or, at a school not required to take attendance, your last documented academically related activity. It then runs the R2T4 calculation.

question: A private foundation is covering my entire cost of attendance for 2026-27. Can I keep my Pell Grant too?
reference_answer: Not if the non-federal aid equals or exceeds your cost of attendance. Starting with 2026-27, the school must either reduce the non-federal aid below your COA or return your Pell Grant and cancel future disbursements. Students eligible for a maximum Pell under the special rule for children of fallen servicemembers or public safety officers are exempt.

question: I'm a freshman and this is my first student loan. Why is it scheduled for late September when class started in August?
must_not_include: something is wrong with your loan
reference_answer: Schools generally can't disburse a Direct Loan to a first-year, first-time borrower until 30 days after the program begins, though some schools with low cohort default rates are exempt. Your aid office can confirm the date.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Vol. 4, Ch. 2: Disbursing Title IV Funds

question: Can you promise the aid office will approve my SAP appeal since I had a medical issue?
reference_answer: No one can promise that; your school decides appeals under its own policy. An illness is a valid basis for an appeal, which must explain why you didn't make SAP and what has changed, ideally with documentation. Ask the financial aid office about its process and deadline.
